domain_assessment.domain: Outpatient orthopedic physical therapy and return-to-sport rehabilitation after ACL reconstruction
domain_assessment.role: Outpatient physical therapist managing an athletic patient's post-operative progression and discharge decisions
domain_assessment.objective: Select safe, appropriately timed rehabilitation progression, testing, clinic-versus-home-program utilization, and return-to-sport recommendations using functional findings and risk information
domain_assessment.incident_type: Nonroutine ACL rehabilitation case involving four judgment-intensive progression, testing, utilization, and clearance decisions

decision_points.summary: At approximately week eight, the PT elects to hold the patient at the existing loading level rather than begin modified plyometric loading.
evidence_before: Quad index of 78% of the uninvolved side
Commonly cited plyometric threshold of approximately 80% to 85%
No pain, swelling, or movement problem
Surgeon clearance was pending but expected
A vivid prior, unrelated early-progression graft re-tear
evidence_after: Reassessment planned for two weeks later
Surgeon clearance subsequently arrives with no structural concerns
goals_constraints: Patient seeks return for competitive soccer preseason
Open-ended authorization has no visit cap or expiration deadline
PT has adequate time to reassess
alternatives: Use a reduced-intensity subset of plyometric work
decision_points.decision_basis: The PT states that the prior patient's graft failure was the deciding influence despite acknowledging that the current patient's findings supported at least partial progression.
decision_points.time_pressure: No insurance-related time pressure; the patient has a sports-season goal but no stated deadline forcing the decision.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate: patient is slightly below a cited threshold but asymptomatic and near threshold.

decision_points.summary: After three uneventful single-leg hopping sessions, the PT delays a scheduled hop-symmetry dynamometer test by one week.
evidence_before: Three pain-free sessions with improving form
No fatigue report or stated clinical red flag
Dynamometer is available only two days per week and slots are scarce
evidence_after: A fourth session is also uneventful
The delayed test costs a dynamometer slot but produces no reported clinical benefit
goals_constraints: Open-ended authorization removes an authorization-expiry concern
alternatives: Delay the test by one week
decision_points.decision_basis: The PT says that because three sessions had gone well, it felt that 'we were due for something to give.'
decision_points.time_pressure: No authorization deadline; scarce testing slots are a logistical constraint but are not stated as the cause of delay.
decision_points.uncertainty: Low-to-moderate: the test result is unknown, but all available session-level indicators are favorable.

decision_points.summary: At approximately week twelve, the PT recommends continuing twice-weekly clinic visits rather than transitioning to a structured home program.
evidence_before: Patient has reached approximately 85% of interim milestones
Functional data could reasonably support either continued clinic treatment or home-program transition
Routine case-manager check-in rather than an expiring authorization review
evidence_after: Patient agrees to continued clinic visits
Patient later reports feeling anxious about stopping because of the PT's wording
goals_constraints: Decide between continued supervised rehabilitation and a home program
Maintain progress while developing patient independence
No visit cap or authorization expiration
alternatives: Transition to a structured home program with check-ins
decision_points.decision_basis: The PT foregrounds possible loss of existing strength gains and gives little attention to the plausible gains from independence and structured home consolidation.
decision_points.time_pressure: No deadline pressure; the authorization context explicitly removes visit-expiration as an explanation.
decision_points.uncertainty: High: the PT explicitly describes the data as genuinely supporting either path.

decision_points.summary: At approximately week sixteen, the PT recommends full return-to-sport clearance and communicates a highly favorable injury-free prognosis without integrating broader re-injury rates.
evidence_before: Scores are among the best the PT has seen in that year's caseload
Patient is returning to a cutting-and-pivoting sport
Patient directly asks about her chances of re-injury
PT says they have familiarity with general post-ACL re-injury frequency
evidence_after: Full clearance is selected instead of a structured reconditioning phase or additional movement screen
The patient receives a risk answer focused on her individual scores rather than population-level re-injury information
alternatives: Clearance with sport-specific reconditioning and closer monitoring
Delay for another functional movement screen
decision_points.decision_basis: The PT converts a favorable personal caseload comparison into a stronger injury-free prediction than the cited scores alone can justify and omits broader risk information when answering the patient's direct question.
decision_points.time_pressure: No pressure to rush clearance; the PT states there was ample authorization runway and enough time to provide a fuller answer.
decision_points.uncertainty: Moderate: strong functional findings are present, but return-to-sport injury risk remains probabilistic and depends on information beyond the two reported indices.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I actually had a case a couple years back — different patient entirely, similar timeline — who progressed into plyometrics early and re-tore her graft. That one stuck with me.” ... “that prior patient's graft failure. I know it's a different case ... but it was vivid enough that it colored how I read this one.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Week-eight progression account and retrospective explanation of the deciding factor
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: A vivid, emotionally salient unrelated adverse outcome is overweighted in the PT's risk weighting for the current patient's progression decision. The PT acknowledges that current objective findings supported at least partial progression, and explicitly rules out authorization pressure.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A clinician may reasonably be conservative around ACL graft loading when a patient is below a cited strength threshold. However, the PT directly attributes the decision to the vivid unrelated re-tear rather than to a patient-specific risk factor or a stated protocol rule.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None for the requested occurrence. A more granular account of the prior case's clinical differences would further distinguish availability-driven aversion from appropriate case-based learning, but is not necessary here.

revision.current_defect: No material defect. The evidence identifies a distinct risk-weighting episode, a salient unrelated memory source, contradictory current-case evidence, and the absence of deadline pressure.
preserve: The 78% quad index and asymptomatic presentation
The explicit absence of authorization pressure
The distinction between full progression, holding, and partial progression
avoid_creating: A second, independent prior-case-based decision episode
A direct textbook label such as 'availability bias'
New patient-specific red flags that would make the conservative decision fully justified

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “Three good sessions in a row is unusual for this stage — felt like we were due for something to give, so I pushed the test back a week rather than run it as scheduled.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Hop-test delay account, followed by the PT's hindsight statement that each session does not owe a contrary outcome based on prior sessions
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The PT treats a short run of favorable, apparently independent sessions as increasing the likelihood that deterioration is due, despite no fatigue, swelling, symptom, PROM, or form-based indicator of imminent decline.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Extra caution could be justified if cumulative loading, fatigue, or unstable movement quality suggested emerging risk. The interview expressly negates those indicators and identifies the streak itself as the reason.

revision.location: Decision point 2, immediately after the description of three clean hopping sessions
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The causal inference from streak to expected reversal is explicit and independently observable.
avoid_creating: New fatigue or symptom indicators that would justify delaying testing
Scheduling or authorization explanations as the primary cause of the delay
Another streak-based decision elsewhere in the interview

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “If we stopped clinic visits now, she'd risk losing the strength gains she'd built up. That's really the framing I led with. I didn't spend much time on the flip side — that a structured home program with check-ins could just as easily consolidate her progress and build her independence.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Week-twelve clinic-versus-home-program discussion with the case manager and patient
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: Under explicitly ambiguous functional evidence, the PT presents the clinic option through avoidance of loss and suppresses an equally plausible gain-framed home-program account. The PT says this framing largely drove the recommendation and affected the patient's response.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Continued supervised care could be clinically preferable for reasons such as adherence risk, sport-specific supervision needs, or demonstrated inability to self-manage. No such individualized reason is supplied; the PT instead identifies framing as the principal driver.

revision.location: Decision point 3, option presentation to the case manager and patient
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The episode contains an ambiguous decision boundary, asymmetric loss-versus-gain presentation, a recommendation shift, and no deadline explanation.
preserve: The fact that either treatment path is clinically plausible
The routine nature of the case-manager contact
avoid_creating: A genuine adherence, safety, or access barrier that independently compels continued clinic treatment
Additional framing episodes at other decision points
An explicit bias label in the participant's own speech

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I told her she was very likely to get back to competitive play injury-free ... based on how strong her numbers were compared to other patients I'd worked with.” ... “I took ‘better than most patients I've seen’ and turned it into ‘very likely injury-free’ more firmly than those two scores alone could really back up.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Week-sixteen discharge and return-to-sport recommendation discussion
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The PT makes an overly favorable individual outcome prediction by translating a favorable personal comparative impression into an insufficiently calibrated assurance of injury-free return. The PT recognizes that the stated certainty exceeds the support provided by the two scores.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Strong hop and quadriceps indices can support favorable return-to-sport expectations. The bias-relevant feature is not optimism alone, but the acknowledged movement from favorable comparative experience to stronger certainty than the available data justify.

revision.location: Decision point 4, initial discharge recommendation before the patient's direct risk question
revision.current_defect: No material defect. This is separable from base-rate neglect because it concerns the PT's affirmative individual-level prediction and personal caseload comparison, not the later omission of population-level statistics.
preserve: The later patient question as a separate probe
avoid_creating: A claim that the test scores alone determine injury-free return
Additional reassurance statements based on unrelated prior cases
Merging the personal-comparison rationale with the population-rate omission

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “She asked what her actual chances were of re-injuring it once she got back to playing. I answered in terms of her numbers ... I didn't really bring in anything about how often athletes in general re-injure after this kind of surgery when they go back to cutting and pivoting sports.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Week-sixteen response to the patient's direct re-injury-risk question
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: When asked for a probability of re-injury, the PT selects only individualized threshold information and omits known, relevant population-level re-injury incidence information. The PT says there was sufficient time to provide a fuller answer and identifies no clinical or organizational barrier.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: A patient's individual risk should be personalized, and broad rates may not perfectly apply without matching covariates. Here, however, the patient asked for her chances after return to a cutting-and-pivoting sport, the PT reports knowing the broader information, and the response used only individual data without explaining the limits of either evidence source.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. Naming the exact type of broader rate, such as an age-, sport-, and graft-relevant re-injury range, would improve ecological detail but is not required to establish the omission mechanism.

revision.location: Decision point 4, answer to the patient's direct question about re-injury probability
revision.current_defect: No material defect. The evidence-selection act is distinct from the optimism instance: this episode concerns omitted population information, whereas cb_04 concerns overconfident use of a personal comparative impression.
preserve: The PT's reliance on individual test thresholds
The PT's stated familiarity with broader re-injury information
The explicit availability of time for a fuller answer
The separation from the preceding clearance recommendation
avoid_creating: A claim that general re-injury rates are irrelevant
A new time-pressure explanation for the omission
Merging this answer with the earlier injury-free assurance into one indistinguishable reasoning trace

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “That one stuck with me.” ... “it was vivid enough that it colored how I read this one.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: A memorable prior graft-failure case becomes disproportionately influential in judging the current patient's risk.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The prior case could represent useful experiential learning if it were clinically comparable and systematically integrated with current evidence. The PT's own statement that the prior case was different and merely vivid favors an availability account.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Very likely to get back to competitive play injury-free” ... “more firmly than those two scores alone could really back up.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The PT expresses confidence exceeding the evidentiary support available from the cited functional measures.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This may be conceptualized as the confidence-calibration component of the intended optimism-bias occurrence rather than a separate accidental instance.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “I didn't spend much time on the flip side — that a structured home program with check-ins could just as easily consolidate her progress and build her independence.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The PT selectively foregrounds evidence consistent with continuing clinic care while neglecting an explicitly plausible alternative interpretation.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This is adequately and more specifically captured as the intended loss/gain framing effect; no independent confirmation-seeking or belief-defense process is demonstrated.

nonbias_cues.cue: The patient is slightly below a commonly cited 80% to 85% plyometric-loading threshold at week eight.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A cautious progression decision can be clinically defensible on this finding alone. It becomes bias-relevant only because the PT explicitly identifies the vivid unrelated graft failure, rather than the threshold or a protocol, as the reason that tipped the choice.

nonbias_cues.cue: The patient wants to return for competitive soccer preseason.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: A performance goal is a legitimate patient-centered objective and creates motivation, not necessarily distorted reasoning. The interview repeatedly distinguishes it from insurance-related deadline pressure.

nonbias_cues.cue: Dynamometer availability is limited to two clinic days and the delay loses a slot.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Limited equipment availability is an organizational constraint. It does not explain the delay here because the PT expressly attributes the decision to expected reversal after a good streak, not logistics.

nonbias_cues.cue: The surgeon clears advanced loading and reports no structural concern.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Specialist clearance is relevant clinical evidence; reliance on it would not itself show bias.

nonbias_cues.cue: The patient compares her progress with a teammate's faster rehabilitation elsewhere.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: This may generate frustration or social comparison, but the interview does not show that it caused the PT's test delay or any other decision.

nonbias_cues.cue: The fourth hopping session is uneventful after the PT's delay.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: The absence of a setback does not establish that the original decision was biased. The supported gambler's-fallacy classification rests on the stated streak-based prediction, not on the unfavorable operational consequence or subsequent outcome.

nonbias_cues.cue: A favorable hop-symmetry and quadriceps index at discharge.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Good functional metrics are legitimate evidence supporting a favorable prognosis. The bias claim rests on the degree and calibration of the injury-free assurance, plus the later omission of population-risk information.

causal_claims.claim: A vivid prior graft-failure memory caused the PT to hold progression despite favorable current findings.
causal_claims.evidence: The PT calls the prior failure the deciding factor and says it would have tipped the decision even with a fixed deadline.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported as the participant's retrospective causal attribution; the text does not independently establish that no legitimate clinical concern also contributed.

causal_claims.claim: A run of three good sessions caused the PT to predict a setback was due and delay testing.
causal_claims.evidence: The PT explicitly links the streak to delaying the test and later disavows the implied dependence between sessions.
causal_claims.assessment: Strongly supported as an in-the-moment reasoning mechanism.

causal_claims.claim: Loss-framed presentation caused the recommendation to continue clinic visits.
causal_claims.evidence: The PT says the framing largely drove the recommendation under data that supported either option.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported as self-reported causal reasoning; the patient's subsequent anxiety is consistent with, but does not alone prove, a framing effect.

causal_claims.claim: Personal comparative impressions caused overconfident injury-free reassurance.
causal_claims.evidence: The PT says the reassurance was based on comparison with other patients and acknowledges that this exceeded what the two scores justified.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported as a calibration failure in the stated prediction.

causal_claims.claim: Individual test data displaced relevant population-level risk information in the patient's risk disclosure.
causal_claims.evidence: The PT reports knowing broader re-injury information but answering only with the patient's threshold-related measures.
causal_claims.assessment: Supported as an evidence-selection omission, subject to normal limits in matching population rates to an individual patient.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The fourth successful session could be read as proving that the test delay was erroneous.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: Do not infer bias from the later outcome; the classification should remain grounded in the PT's explicit 'due for something to give' reasoning.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: The patient's anxiety after the clinic-versus-home discussion could be read as proving that framing caused the recommendation.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: Treat the patient's response as corroborative impact evidence, not the sole proof. The PT's account of asymmetric framing and its influence on the recommendation is the primary evidence.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Favorable discharge scores could be read as disproving optimism bias.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: The relevant issue is probability calibration and the scope of the injury-free claim, not whether the patient had favorable metrics.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Insurance-authorization visit-window constraint: the scenario uses open-ended authorization with no fixed visit cap or expiration deadline, rather than a capped fixed-duration authorization.
held_constant: Patient identity, competitive soccer goal, and motivation to return for preseason
ACL reconstruction context and clinical values at all four checkpoints
Dynamometer availability on only two clinic days
The sequence and substantive content of the four decision points
causal_audit.explanation: The interview consistently isolates the intended counterfactual variable. It establishes no visit cap or expiration at the outset, labels the case-manager contact routine, and directly probes whether authorization pressure affected each relevant decision. The participant consistently denies authorization-clock influence while retaining the planned cognitive mechanisms. The patient's preseason goal and limited dynamometer scheduling remain plausible background constraints, but the transcript does not use them as alternative causes of the five targeted mechanisms.

global_revision_constraints: Preserve the open-ended authorization and explicit absence of visit-window pressure; this is the causal intervention being tested.
Maintain the separation between the discharge reassurance based on personal comparative impression and the later response that omits population-level re-injury information.
Do not count alternative labels for the same evidence trace, including availability heuristic at decision point 1 and overconfidence at decision point 4, as additional accidental occurrences.

If later editing is undertaken for naturalness, retain the explicit reasoning mechanisms and absence-of-deadline probes; reducing those details would risk weakening otherwise well-supported target instances.
